chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Sa'd ibn Muslim from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I not inform you about the one whom the Fire will be forbidden for tomorrow?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The easy-going, the close/kind, the gentle, the simple.'

key_terms.السَّهْلُ: The simple, one who is uncomplicated and easy to deal with
key_terms.اللَّیِّنُ: The gentle, one with a soft temperament
key_terms.الْقَرِیبُ: The close/kind, one who is approachable and affectionate
key_terms.الْهَیِّنُ: The easy-going, one who is not harsh or difficult
key_terms.تَحْرُمُ عَلَیْهِ النَّارُ: The Fire will be forbidden for him (guaranteed entry to Paradise)

ai.seo_question: What are the four character traits that protect a person from the Hellfire according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of Shaykh al-Saduq, this hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (character) as a primary determinant of spiritual success, linking inner humility to external social ease. The four traits—gentleness, approachability, softness, and simplicity—reflect the Prophetic model of avoiding arrogance and rigidity, a concept deeply resonant with the Shia understanding of the Ahl al-Bayt’s demeanor. This narration serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate a disposition that naturally repels the harshness of the Hellfire through consistent, gentle interaction with others.
